newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate climbs to 11.5 vs 10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate climbs to 11.5 vs 10.9 pct.

text.p: Strong demand by bank borrowers lifted the Croatian average lending rate to 11.5 percent on Monday from 10.9 percent, and money market dealers predicted a further rate increase amid strained kuna liquidity.
The weighted interbank call money rate already rose to 11.2 from 10.5 percent, but term rates were mostly steady at up to 16 percent for one-month loans.
Dealers put settlements at a low 20 million kuna, including some 8.3 million renewed deals.
The kuna supply bottomed at 23 million kuna as bank accounts emptied due to statutory reserve payment.
The central bank also called repayment of some 33 million repo funds and will drain another 116 million on Tuesday.
The kuna midrate for Tuesday eased further to 6.0357 versus the dollar but firmed slightly to 3.5630 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
